subject: Human Evolution
title: The Savanna Hypothesis
description: A 60-second lesson on The Savanna Hypothesis.

hook.text: When forests shrank and grasslands spread, our ancestors faced a choice: stay in the trees or stand up.

buildup.text: Standing upright lets you see over tall grass—spotting predators and prey across the open savanna.

discovery.text: This 'savanna hypothesis' dominated for decades: bipedalism was Africa's grassland solution.

twist.text: But early bipedal fossils are found in woodland, not grassland. The timing doesn't quite fit.

climax.text: Savanna life may have refined bipedalism, but it probably started in the trees, not the plains.

punchline.text: We stood up before the grass grew tall.

quiz.question: What challenge does the savanna hypothesis face?
options: Early bipedal fossils are found in woodland
Grass is too short to need standing
